extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and prospective NIDDK grant applicants (investigators, trainees, small businesses) seeking NIDDK funding/program contacts
extracted.subtask_short: finding NIDDK funding programs and contacts
extracted.subtask_description: Locate NIDDK research funding programs organized by disease area, identify relevant program titles and staff contacts, and learn preparatory/administrative steps required to apply. Includes program-specific entry-points (training, SBIR/STTR, human subjects, translational research) and resource pointers (dkNET, NIH Common Fund).

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize search by disease area
rubrics_metrics.description: NIDDK research funding programs are located below, organized by the disease area they cover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Click to expand a disease area, then select a program title for more information, including staff contacts, goals, and activities. Use the disease-area organization to find programs most relevant to your work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use program staff contacts to learn priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: You may find this information useful if you need to: speak to someone about funding opportunities in your research area; learn about NIDDK funding priorities and key people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and contact listed program staff to clarify funding priorities, program goals, and appropriate funding mechanisms before preparing an application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register early at eRA Commons and grants.gov
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration is required at eRA Commons and grants.gov and can take 4 weeks. Complete registrations well in advance of grant deadlines to avoid administrative barriers to submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training program eligibility and goals
rubrics_metrics.description: NIDDK supports the training and career development of medical and graduate students, postdoctoral fellows, and physician scientists through institutional and individual grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use NIDDK training program pages to learn about eligible trainees, career-development aims, and application mechanisms for institutional vs individual awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small business (SBIR/STTR) funding focus
rubrics_metrics.description: NIDDK participates in the Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) and Small Business Technology Transfer (STTR) programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These programs support innovative research conducted by small businesses that has the potential for commercialization. Consult program contacts to determine fit and commercialization expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subjects / clinical research funding scope
rubrics_metrics.description: NIDDK provides funding for pivotal clinical research, from preliminary clinical feasibility to large multi-center studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proposing human subjects research, review NIDDK clinical research pages for expectations around study scale (feasibility through multicenter), regulatory requirements, and appropriate programmatic contacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translational research emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: NIDDK provides funding opportunities and resources to encourage translation of basic discoveries into novel therapeutics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translational research applicants should consult NIDDK translational program resources and contacts to align applications with translational milestones, preclinical/clinical transition expectations, and available support mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: dkNET resources for rigor and data
rubrics_metrics.description: dkNET supports researchers with tools to enhance scientific rigor, reproducibility, and transparency, and provides a big data knowledge base for genomic and pathway hypothesis generation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use dkNET to find resources, datasets, and tools that can strengthen proposals' rigor, reproducibility plans, and data-analysis approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use NIDDK meetings & workshops for community and updates
rubrics_metrics.description: NIDDK lists Meetings & Workshops (events, webinars) related to programmatic topics and community engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend relevant NIDDK-sponsored meetings or webinars (e.g., Pathway to Kidney Recovery, Accelerating the Translation of Cell Therapy) to learn about program priorities, network with program staff, and gather information useful for applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult related NIH resources (NIH Common Fund and Research at NIDDK)
rubrics_metrics.description: For NIDDK research activities at NIH facilities or cross-cutting NIH initiatives, the page points to Research at NIDDK and the NIH Common Fund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your work involves NIH facilities (Maryland, Arizona) or overlaps with Common Fund projects, consult those resources for site-specific policies, available opportunities, and cross-institute funding mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program- and topic-specific listings (detailed program names)
rubrics_metrics.description: The page enumerates many specific program areas and centers (e.g., Diabetes; Digestive Diseases; Kidney Disease; Nutrition; Obesity; Pancreatic Disease; Urologic Diseases; Cystic Fibrosis; Hematologic Diseases; Bioengineering, Biotechnology, and Imaging; Genetics and Genomics; Clinical Research and Epidemiology; Research Core Centers; etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each listed program/title, click through to view staff contacts, goals, activities, and any program-specific funding mechanisms or application guidance. Use these topic-specific pages to match your proposal to the correct program.
